text:
ara: Heads up — found temporary AWS session creds embedded inside a support attachment that was uploaded to a presigned S3 URL. Bucket: redwood-internal-support-uploads. Role: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/support-assume-role. Creds expire ~6h but we should contain now.
ben-platform: Ack. Can you paste the exact object/key and URL so I can revoke the presigned link?
ara: object: support-2026-03-19-logbundle.zip — presigned link removed from the ticket. @ben-platform already deleted the presigned URL. But we need to assume the creds could have been used upstream.
chao: Two immediate containment options: (A) temporarily modify the role trust policy to block AssumeRole, (B) detach all policies from the role (removes permissions). (A) has less infra churn, (B) guaranteed no permissions. Thoughts?
dina-devex: prefer (A) to avoid breaking CI that assumes the role. Make the block explicit and keep a short maintenance window. Also need a list of apps using this role to update their Vault mappings.
ara: Proposed short plan: 1) cut presigned URL (done) 2) apply temporary Deny to role trust policy to stop new sessions 3) search CloudTrail and ALB/S3 access logs for actions using that role 4) rotate any long-lived IAM users that can assume this role 5) update Vault role mapping and re-issue creds / re-enable trust 6) run smoke tests and re-enable.
chao: I'll apply a temporary assume-role deny. Command I'll run:
```bash
# create policy file deny-assume-temporary.json then:
aws iam update-assume-role-policy --role-name support-assume-role --policy-document file://deny-assume-temporary.json
```
deny-assume-temporary.json will be a policy that denies sts:AssumeRole for principals except for an allowlist.
leo-sre: Also run CloudTrail lookup for events where userIdentity.arn contains support-assume-role and timeframe +/-1h from object upload:
```bash
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=support-assume-role --start-time 2026-03-19T10:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-19T16:00:00Z
```
and query S3 access logs for the presigned URL IPs. I'll add IDS alerts for those IPs.
ben-platform: On it — starting CloudTrail + S3 logs search now. ETA ~20m. If we see API activity from unknown IPs, we'll escalate to incident response.
vault-bot: vault: noticed the role is referenced at secret path: secret/aws/roles/support-assume-role (lease duration 1h). Recommend rotating the backend role binding and re-issuing leases after containment.
dina-devex: I will gather a quick inventory of consumers (CI jobs, support workers, ingestion pipelines). If we rotate the Vault mapping name, we need to update consumers. I'll post a short list in 30m.
ara: Decision: chao proceed with trust-policy deny. chao, please add a temporary allow for our SRE IPs so we can run diagnostics. After deny, we move to searching logs then decide whether to rotate underlying IAM users or create replacement role.
chao: Doing it now. Patch applied. Added allow for 3 SRE IPs.
deploy-bot: CI pipelines referencing role support-assume-role have been paused by @deploy-bot.
ben-platform: CloudTrail results: 3 AssumeRole calls in the window from an IP in region us-west-2 that we don't recognize. Actions observed: s3:GetObject on redwood-internal-support-uploads. Marking those sessions as suspicious.
leo-sre: Add CloudWatch metric filter for AssumeRole calls for this principal and fire an alert to #incidents if rate > 1/min for 10m.
ara: We'll treat this as a credential exposure incident. Next steps: (A) keep role trust blocked, (B) rotate any IAM user keys that could assume the role (list in inventory), (C) rotate Vault backend bindings and re-issue leases, (D) run a full search for the creds in public repos, support tickets, and S3 buckets using our DLP tooling.
dina-devex: I found two CI jobs and one support lambda that assume the role. I'll open PRs to switch them to a new Vault role alias.
ben-platform: I've exported the CloudTrail event IDs and copied suspect IPs to the security incident doc. Will hand off to infra for possible abuse takedown.
chao: After we validate there's no lateral movement, plan is to re-enable trust using new external-id requirement and rotate the Vault role binding. I'll coordinate with @dina-devex for the exact mapping change.
vault-bot: vault: revoked all active leases for secret/aws/roles/support-assume-role — 8 leases revoked.
leo-sre: Confirmed no additional unusual EC2 activity. We'll keep network flow capture for 24h.
ara: Thanks all. Actions assigned: ben-platform: logs + IP takedown; chao: trust-policy block + re-enable plan; dina-devex: consumer inventory + PRs; leo-sre: alerts + monitoring; I'll draft the incident summary + timeline and post to security board. Everyone confirm when tasks are done here. :eyes: :thumbsup:
ben-platform: done with initial log sweep, uploading notes to the incident doc.
dina-devex: inventory posted, PRs opened (refs in incident doc).
chao: trust policy reverted to new policy that requires external-id and we rotated role binding in Vault. Leaving the role disabled until daytime maintenance window tomorrow 16:00 UTC.
leo-sre: Monitoring alerts in place. Will keep watch and escalate if anything else shows up.
ara: Closing the thread for active action — will open a follow-up postmortem ticket and schedule a rotation sweep for other high-risk roles. Great job everyone. :white_check_mark:
